quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: When a car is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to give yourself more space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to give yourself more space.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, ride in a way that makes it easy for them to pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid a crash?

options.text: Make sure other drivers can see you.
Keep your plans hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Stay visible to other drivers by using signals and brake lights. Use your lane position wisely. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Where should you ride when following a car?

options.text: In the part closest to the shoulder.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more than their side mirrors, so this position makes it more likely they will notice you.

questions.question: When you are stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Do not check your rearview mirrors.
Look for chances to squeeze through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay back from the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the car backs up or if a vehicle approaches too quickly from behind.

questions.question: If you have been drinking alcohol, what should you do?

options.text: Decide based on how you feel after drinking.
Set a drinking limit beforehand so you can ride safely.

questions.explanation: The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol. Even small amounts can affect your riding ability.

questions.question: How should you handle a tailgater?

options.text: Let them pass by slowing down or changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass by slowing down or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: If safe, change lanes or slow down to let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Riding a motorcycle is ______ driving a car.
questions.explanation: Riding a motorcycle is more tiring than driving a car, especially on long trips. Do not ride when tired. Fatigue reduces your control of the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which material gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the most protection when riding.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing where to ride in a lane?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which lane position will make your trip shorter.
If you can pass more vehicles in one position than another.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Also make sure you have enough space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles. They often occur within the first few minutes of riding.

questions.question: If you think stopping your motorcycle will take longer than usual, you should:
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle takes longer to stop, give yourself more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is that:

options.text: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will run like new for years. Regular maintenance should be part of your routine care.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: If wearing laced footwear while riding, the laces should:
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces securely while riding so they don't catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: You can reduce serious injury in a crash by wearing:
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face during a crash.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle:

options.text: Allows the engine to slow the motorcycle.
Should not be done around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows the engine to slow the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through downshifting helps slow your motorcycle. If you use engine braking, use your brake lights so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Leave their blind spot as fast as possible.
Slow down in the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave their blind spot as fast as possible.
questions.explanation: Get out of another vehicle's blind spot quickly. Move into the passing lane and accelerate past the vehicle.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only happen on long trips.
Should be part of your regular scanning.
Are not helpful because you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly as part of your normal scanning. Also check mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Besides hazardous road conditions, what should riders look for?

options.text: Oncoming traffic that might turn left in front of you.
Traffic entering from side roads on the left and right.

questions.explanation: Riders should constantly look ahead, to the sides, and behind their motorcycles. Watch for hazardous road conditions and traffic that could become dangerous.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes moving in the same direction are about to become one lane.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear to be seen on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green make you easier to see while riding. Wear bright clothing no matter what time of day you ride.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what may you need to adjust?
questions.explanation: Add a few pounds of pressure to your tires when carrying a passenger. Also adjust the suspension to handle the extra weight.

questions.question: What must you have to carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two riders.
You should not give the passenger protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Do not carry a passenger unless your motorcycle has a seat for two riders. The motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.

questions.question: What is the best source of information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding a motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are borrowing a motorcycle.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Attach a large flag to its frame.
Ride with the headlight turned on.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with the headlight turned on.
questions.explanation: Make yourself easier to see by wearing bright, reflective clothing. Ride with your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane helps the driver see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
Wind may prevent the use of a side mirror.
Side mirrors should not be used by drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chances of an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in and not be noticed by other drivers.
Don't use turn signals unless riding at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride closely behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Signal your intentions with turn signals, brake light, and lane position. Keep a safe distance, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle beside you.
Other drivers may need to use that lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The driver won't know you are there. The vehicle may also block your path of escape if another hazard appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. Turning left at this sign is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Drive slowly and carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Stay farther away from the vehicle in front of you.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not tell the passenger about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle behaves differently with a passenger's weight. You need more space behind the vehicle in front of you to stop safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is put on the back of vehicles moving slower than 25 mph. These include farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: You should increase the space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: Conditions make it harder to stop.
You want to look at the scenery.
You want other drivers to cut in front of you.
You want to hide from the driver in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions make it harder to stop.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when stopping is harder than normal. This includes wet roads, poor visibility around the vehicle ahead, or heavy traffic where drivers may cut in front of you.

questions.question: The only way to become sober after drinking is to:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: To check tire pressure, you should:

options.text: Compare it to another tire's height.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge before every ride. An under-inflated tire may look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear durable pants and a jacket that cover your arms and legs. If you crash, exposed skin can be badly injured.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow and black. They tell you about road hazards ahead. This sign means a lane is ending and you need to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, clean your mirrors and adjust them properly. You may see your arm or shoulder in the mirror, but you need to see the road behind and beside you.
